w:r.w:t: A step-by-step guide for demonstrating the graduate student lifecycle:
admission handoff • course offering & adjustment • enrollment • research & defense • practicum • graduation • standing changes
Every demo account password is: DemoPass123!

The Graduate School Lifecycle Portal is a web application that gives the University of St. La Salle (USLS) Graduate School a single, consolidated workspace for monitoring and coordinating the full graduate student lifecycle. It replaces the manual, spreadsheet-only process the Graduate School currently uses to track where each student stands.

The application does not replace AIMS, the university's official academic information system. AIMS remains the official source for student identity, enrollment, enrolled subjects, grades, and course completion. Authorized staff export an approved monitoring workbook and import it here; those official values are shown as read-only and are labeled with their source. The portal adds the coordination, decision-support, and exception-reporting layer on top of that official data.
What the portal lets staff do
Import the Academic Coordinator monitoring sheet and reconcile it into a single student list.
Set up the subjects offered for a specific semester, together with the schedule and the assigned faculty member.
Tag students as enrolled in offered subjects, either by uploading a class list or by searching a single student.
Identify which subjects are needed next term and which students are affected if a subject is not offered.
Route research submissions, panel matching, and defense scheduling for each student.
Process standing changes: subject withdrawal, leave of absence, readmission, AWOL, and residency.
Track graduation eligibility and prepare the Dean-approved endorsement list.
To run the demonstration smoothly, the presenting machine should meet the following:
A modern browser (Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge recommended), kept up to date.
At least 4 GB of RAM and a few GB of free disk space for the local database and demo files.
Python 3 and Node.js installed, so the backend server and the built front-end can run locally.
The demonstration runs locally on the presenter's machine; a live internet connection is only needed for the optional Policy Assistant feature.

On the first start, the system automatically prepares its demonstration database and seeds all of the demo accounts and sample records described in this document. This runs once and may take a short moment. If a demo account or the login dropdown ever appears empty, restarting the server re-seeds the demonstration data.
Start-up sequence (performed once before the demo):
Build the front-end so the latest screens are served.
Start the application server. The system seeds the demonstration data automatically on first run.
Open the application in the browser at the local address shown when the server starts (the portal runs on port 5050).
You will land on the Login screen. Use the accounts in Section 4.

Additional seeded students exist for handoff, course adjustments, readmission, AWOL, residency, and a second student for practicum and graduation, so every list and batch screen has more than one example.
After logging in, the left sidebar is grouped into sections. The graduate lifecycle is presented as a numbered sequence so the demonstration can move through it in order.
1 · Student Handoff — import and reconcile the monitoring sheet.
2 · Course Adjustments — set up subject offerings and review subject needs.
3 · Enrollment — tag students to offered subjects.
4 · Research Gate — check each student's required research submissions.
5 · Panel Matching — recommend and finalize the defense panel.
6 · Defense Scheduling — find a common defense slot.
7 · Practicum — track practicum requirements and hours.
8 · Graduation — check eligibility and prepare the endorsement list.
Students, Faculty, Monitoring Sheet, Enrollment Class List

Each scenario below is self-contained: it names the account to use, the story behind it, the data to enter, and the steps to follow. Run them in order for a full end-to-end demonstration, or pick individual scenarios.
The matrix below confirms where each requested screen or workflow is demonstrated. The detailed steps then follow the same sequence as the portal.

Scenario 1 — Import and reconcile the monitoring sheet

At the start of the term break, Graduate School Staff receive the Academic Coordinator monitoring workbook. Grace Fernandez imports it, checks the reconciliation result, and verifies that the Monitoring Sheet and Student Records show the same official source data.
From the sidebar, open 1 · Student Handoff.
Click Browse files under Import from the monitoring sheet, select the MAED workbook, then click Import students.
Review the import summary and validation items. Existing students are updated, genuinely new students are added, and conflicting or incomplete source rows remain visible for reconciliation.
Review Upload history. Each workbook version is preserved with its time, file name, counts, validation result, and conflict record.

Open Monitoring Sheet. Choose MAED and the relevant semester, use the progress/risk/enrollment filters, and verify the read-only curriculum grid. Use Flag issue to record a discrepancy without overwriting the source.
Open Students, search for Sofia Reyes or Anton Bautista, and open the full student record. Verify identity, program, standing, enrollment, coursework, tasks, activity, and source references.
If an official value is wrong, correct it in the authorized source and re-import the workbook; do not manually rewrite the imported value here.

The imported values (identity, program, completed subjects) are read-only and labeled with their source. If a value looks wrong, staff use Flag issue to record a discrepancy — the portal never edits an official value directly.

Scenario 2 — Review faculty records and set up semester offerings

Before enrollment opens, Academic Coordinator Dr. Ramon Alvarez reviews faculty profiles, studies live subject demand, decides what to offer, routes the plan for approval, publishes it, and completes each offering's faculty, schedule, and section.
MAED — Master of Arts in Education
Choose a MAED subject surfaced by the demand report
Choose after reviewing the faculty profile and workload
Open Faculty. Search for a faculty member, open the profile, and review specialization, preferred teaching subjects, login email, current load, weekly availability, and calendar source.
Open 2 · Course Adjustments and stay on Demand & adjustments. Select MAED and the planning semester.
Review the automatically calculated subject needs and affected-student counts. These figures support the decision; they do not publish a subject or assign faculty automatically.
Mark the chosen subjects as offered, set the section count and faculty choice, then click Save draft.
Click Submit for approval. Sign in as the Dean to approve or return the plan, then return as the Academic Coordinator and click Publish after approval.
Switch to Offering setup. Complete or confirm the assigned faculty, schedule, and section for each published subject, then click Save.
Faculty suggestions and preferences are advisory. The Academic Coordinator owns the final assignment, and only published official offerings become available in Enrollment.

Scenario 4 — See which subjects are needed and who will be affected

The Academic Coordinator needs evidence for the next offering decision. The Subject-needs report calculates remaining requirements from current student records and identifies each student who may be delayed if a subject is withheld.
Open 2 · Course Adjustments and select Demand & adjustments.
Choose the Program and planning semester. Review Students reviewed, Subjects with need, and Student-subject needs.
In the Subject-needs report, compare Students needing with Not taken. Completed, taken, and currently enrolled subjects are excluded.
Read the Affected students column for the names, student numbers, and delay impact behind the count. A single student need is enough to surface a subject.
Use the evidence to revise the offering draft, then follow the submit → Dean approval → publish sequence from Scenario 2.
The report is recalculated from current records; it is decision support, not an automatic offering or faculty assignment.

Elena Navarro requests to withdraw from one enrolled subject before classes begin or during the first seven calendar days of class. GS Staff forwards the request, the Dean approves it, and GS Staff tags only the selected subject as Withdrawn. The student remains Active, the other subjects remain unchanged, and the withdrawn subject produces no grade, academic penalty, or adverse transcript mark.
Joshua Lim demonstrates the unusual case: the Dean denies his request. The system preserves his enrollment, prevents the subject-withdrawal tagging and export steps, and informs him of the decision.

Graduation candidates reviewed and approved for endorsement.
Students appear on the Graduation page only when coursework, research stages, defense results, post-defense completion documents, and any required practicum are complete.
However, being academically eligible does not automatically allow batch selection:

After submitting the signed application PDF, the student moves to Step 2 · Application Submitted — Ready for Batch Creation.
Only students in Step 2 can be selected for a graduation batch.

Scenario 13 — Standing changes: LOA, Readmission, AWOL return, and Residency

Standing changes are separate governed flows. Leave of Absence pauses an active student; Readmission restores a student after approved LOA; AWOL is created automatically from explicit source evidence; Return from AWOL requires written intent and a Dean decision; and Residency records valid academic work without subjects.
As Daniel Fernandez, open Leave of Absence and enter the effective start semester, effective end semester, reason category, and remarks. Submit the structured application.

As Graduate School Staff, open Leave of Absence, select the submitted request, run the deterministic policy checker, and review the requested period, reason, prior approved leaves, and minimum residency.
Complete the staff review and forward the request to the Dean. A policy recommendation supports the review but does not approve the request.
As the Dean, open LOA / Readmission / AWOL and approve, deny, or return the case. Approval changes the student to On Leave / LOA and enables the Registrar report.

For an accurate demonstration, keep these points in mind and state them plainly if asked:

AIMS is a separate, official university system. This portal does not connect to AIMS live; it uses an approved export/import workbook. Imported official values are read-only here, and corrections are made in AIMS and re-imported.
The application records and displays enrollment; it does not perform official enrollment in place of the Registrar.
Grades and course-completion come from the official export, not from manual entry inside the portal.
Risk is shown as Not Yet Assessed for new or incomplete records instead of an invented Low/Medium/High score, until the official risk rules are confirmed.
Where the portal shows recommendations (subject needs, faculty, panels), they are suggestions with a stated basis that an authorized person confirms.
The Policy Assistant answers from the provided handbook and research documents; treat it as decision support, not an official ruling.
